'''Lévy's modulus of continuity theorem''' is a [[theorem]] that gives a result about an [[almost surely|almost sure]] behaviour of an estimate of the [[modulus of continuity]] for [[Wiener process]], that is used to model what's known as [[Brownian motion]].

Lévy's modulus of continuity theorem is named after the French mathematician [[Paul Lévy (mathematician)|Paul Lévy]].

== Statement of the result ==
Let <math>B : [0, 1] \times \Omega \to \mathbb{R}</math> be a standard Wiener process. Then, [[almost surely]],

:<math>\lim_{h \to 0} \sup_{t, t'\leq 1; |t-t'|\leq h } \frac{| B_{t'} - B_{t} |}{\sqrt{2 h \log (1 / h)}} = 1.</math>

In other words, the [[sample path]]s of Brownian motion have modulus of continuity

:<math>\omega_{B} (\delta) = c\sqrt{2 \delta \log (1 / \delta)}</math>

with probability one, for <math>c > 1</math> and sufficiently small <math>\delta > 0</math>.<ref>Lévy, P. Author Profile Théorie de l’addition des variables aléatoires. 2. éd. (French) page 172 Zbl 0056.35903 (Monographies des probabilités.) Paris: Gauthier-Villars, XX, 387 p. (1954)</ref>
